items.title: T-05. Test Every Detail
items.reviewQuestion: Reassess if a stable user-facing contract is introduced that requires snapshot coverage.
items.scope: Repository-wide test policy; no published content, URLs, or frontmatter are changed.

evidence.verification: npm run audit:quality-contracts && npm run verify:release
evidence.result: The repository tests stable contracts (routes, metadata, relations, search, assets, and security boundaries) rather than full HTML snapshots; the quality contract audit passed 20/20 and the release gate passed.

items.residualRisk: A newly introduced stable rendering contract could need focused snapshot or structural assertions; unrestricted full-page snapshots remain intentionally out of scope.

items.title: T-06. Utility-Only Unit Tests
items.reviewQuestion: Reassess if future tests bypass the content-to-artifact path and cover utilities only.
items.scope: Repository-wide integration quality contract; no published content, URLs, or frontmatter are changed.

evidence.verification: npm run verify:release && npm run audit:quality-contracts
evidence.result: The release contract exercises content classification, relations, internal links, search, static build, admin boundaries, and generated artifacts together; quality contracts passed 20/20 and the release gate passed.

items.residualRisk: The release gate is integration-oriented but does not replace targeted unit tests for every helper; new helpers still need focused regression cases when their contracts are introduced.

items.title: T-07. Mock Everything
items.reviewQuestion: Reassess if a new test suite replaces real corpus and artifact checks with mocked filesystem or parser inputs.
items.scope: Repository-wide fixture and integration policy; no published content, URLs, or frontmatter are changed.

evidence.result: Release verification reads the repository's real Markdown corpus, YAML frontmatter, link graph, generated dist artifact, and admin boundary; it does not rely exclusively on mocked filesystem or parser data.

items.residualRisk: Small in-memory fixtures remain appropriate for focused search and negative-path cases; they must supplement, not replace, real-corpus and artifact checks.

items.title: T-10. Fixture Does Not Resemble Real Content
items.reviewQuestion: Reassess if a new checker is validated only against synthetic content without representative corpus coverage.
items.scope: Repository-wide representative-content verification; no published content, URLs, or frontmatter are changed.

evidence.result: The release gate validates the representative production corpus (3,387 Markdown documents) for frontmatter, classification, links, relations, search, build output, and security boundaries rather than relying only on minimal synthetic fixtures.

items.residualRisk: Targeted parser edge cases still benefit from small fixtures; fixture additions must preserve representative headings, math, directives, code fences, images, and frontmatter combinations.

items.title: T-100. Testing System Becomes the Product
items.reviewQuestion: Reassess if quality tooling grows beyond the risk-weighted contracts needed to protect publishing and content integrity.
items.scope: Repository quality-governance scope; no published content, URLs, or frontmatter are changed.

evidence.verification: npm run audit:quality-contracts && npm run verify:release && npm run audit:tooling
evidence.result: The repository maintains a bounded set of risk-based quality contracts (20/20 passing), a single release gate, and tooling inventory checks; the system does not attempt exhaustive prose or pixel assertions.

items.residualRisk: A growing script inventory can still increase maintenance cost; new checks should include a failure-impact rationale and retire redundant contracts.

items.title: T-11. Fixture Copy of Production Article
items.reviewQuestion: Reassess if a test introduces a copied production article; replace it with a minimal behavior fixture or direct corpus coverage.
items.scope: Repository fixture maintenance policy; no published content, URLs, or frontmatter are changed.

evidence.result: Focused search cases use small in-memory records, while corpus and artifact audits read production Markdown directly; no copied production article is maintained as a separate fixture.

items.residualRisk: A future fixture can drift if it grows into a full article; keep fixtures minimal and retain direct real-corpus coverage for integration checks.

items.title: T-12. Unit Test Internal Implementation
items.reviewQuestion: Reassess if future tests assert private helper names, call order, or implementation-specific DOM structure instead of observable contracts.
items.scope: Repository-wide black-box quality contract; no published content, URLs, or frontmatter are changed.

evidence.verification: npm run verify:search && npm run test:relations && npm run audit:links && npm run audit:quality-contracts
evidence.result: The quality checks assert observable search, relation, link, and contract outcomes; they do not mock or assert private helper call order or internal implementation details.

items.residualRisk: Implementation regressions that preserve current outputs may evade black-box checks; add focused contract assertions when a user-visible behavior is introduced.

items.title: T-13. Generated HTML String Equality
items.reviewQuestion: Reassess if a stable HTML contract is introduced; assert selected structure or semantics rather than formatting-sensitive full strings.
items.scope: Repository-wide rendered-output test policy; no published content, URLs, or frontmatter are changed.

evidence.verification: npm run audit:quality-contracts && npm run verify:release
evidence.result: Rendered output is checked through semantic contracts, asset structure, security boundaries, and successful static generation; formatting-sensitive full HTML string equality is intentionally not used.

items.residualRisk: A semantic regression can pass if no existing contract covers it; new user-visible HTML behavior requires a focused structural assertion or accessibility check.

items.title: T-14. Locale-Dependent Test
items.reviewQuestion: Reassess with AP-P-77 if a build or test result changes across Node ICU/default locale settings.
items.scope: Quality-test determinism policy; no published content, URLs, or frontmatter are changed.

evidence.verification: npm run verify:release && npm run audit:quality-contracts
evidence.result: Search and release checks assert stable semantic outcomes; generated LLM artifacts use explicit English ordering, while user-facing Korean label sorting remains an intentional presentation concern rather than a test oracle.

items.residualRisk: Some user-facing localeCompare calls intentionally follow locale semantics, and unqualified ordering in auxiliary paths could vary across ICU environments; add an explicit locale or key-based comparator when such a path becomes a release invariant.

items.title: T-15. Time-Dependent Test
items.reviewQuestion: Reassess if a test begins comparing against the wall clock or an unseeded current date instead of explicit input timestamps.
items.scope: Repository-wide temporal determinism policy; no published content, URLs, or frontmatter are changed.

evidence.result: Search, relation, series, and release checks compare explicit document dates and deterministic outcomes; current time is used only for report metadata or runtime admin behavior, not as a test oracle.

items.residualRisk: Admin runtime features intentionally depend on current time; those paths require injected clocks or bounded tolerance if promoted into automated tests.

items.title: T-27. Every External Link on Every Commit
items.reviewQuestion: Reassess external-link sampling on scheduled runs or before releases when freshness evidence is required.
items.scope: Repository publish-gate network policy; no published content, URLs, or frontmatter are changed.

evidence.verification: npm run verify:release && npm run audit:links
evidence.result: The release gate checks the local internal link graph and build artifact; external freshness is an explicit opt-in audit rather than a network-dependent per-commit blocker.

items.residualRisk: External URLs can expire between scheduled audits; run the upstream freshness audit before releases that depend on third-party references.

items.title: T-28. External Failure Blocks Publishing
items.reviewQuestion: Reassess each external gate by impact: security and artifact integrity remain blocking; advisory freshness checks remain non-blocking.
items.scope: Repository release-gate failure policy; no published content, URLs, or frontmatter are changed.

evidence.result: The release gate intentionally blocks on dependency security audit, build, secret, and artifact-boundary failures; external reference freshness is kept outside the blocking path. This preserves fail-closed security behavior without making advisory network checks mandatory.

items.residualRisk: A provider outage can delay releases when a security or integrity verdict cannot be obtained; use the cached/offline audit only as diagnosis, not as a silent bypass.

items.title: T-29. Redirect Considered Healthy Forever
items.reviewQuestion: Reassess redirect targets and fallback links when routes or canonical URLs change.
items.scope: Repository redirect safety contract; no published content, URLs, or frontmatter are changed.

evidence.verification: npm run audit:product-experience && npm run verify:release
evidence.result: Redirect routes are audited for noindex, canonicalization, and a manual fallback link; redirect presence alone is not treated as permanent health. Product experience audit passed 10/10.

items.residualRisk: A redirect can still point to a semantically obsolete destination; periodic content-owner review remains necessary for long-lived redirects.
